title: service-mesh-identity-proofing-and-evidence-standard-2026
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview
=======
This document defines the standard for identity proofing, evidence collection, and retention for service-to-service identities (mTLS certificates, SPIFFE/SPIRE identities, Kubernetes service accounts, and short-lived cloud tokens) when traffic is routed through the Redwood service mesh. It clarifies the minimal evidence package required for compliance audits, the retention classification for each artifact, owner responsibilities, and automated collection recipes.

Audience
--------
- Security Engineers
- Platform / SRE teams owning the service mesh or identity broker
- Compliance and Audit teams
- Incident Response leads

Goals and non-goals
-------------------
- Goals:
  - Provide a reproducible evidence package for identity lifecycle events (issuance, rotation, revocation, anomaly detection)
  - Ensure evidence meets audit requirements for data residency and tamper-resistance
  - Define retention classes aligned to legal and operational needs
- Non-goals:
  - Replacing cloud provider IAM guides; this is a Redwood-specific overlay for mesh identities
  - Prescribing a single implementation — recipes for SPIRE, Istio, and cloud-native token flows are included as examples

Scope and terminology
---------------------
- Identity types covered: mTLS certs issued by Mesh PKI, SPIFFE IDs, Kubernetes service accounts (token-based), and short-lived cloud IAM tokens used by sidecars.
- Evidence package: the set of logs, artifacts, and cryptographic proofs required to demonstrate control and timing of identity operations.
- Retention classes: EPHEMERAL (7 days), OPERATIONAL (90 days), COMPLIANCE (3 years), LEGAL_HOLD (indefinite)

Minimal evidence package (per identity event)
-------------------------------------------
Each identity lifecycle event (issue, rotate, revoke) must be accompanied by the following artifacts: 
1) Event metadata record (Operational JSON) — fields: event_id, identity_subject, event_type, issuer_id, timestamp_utc, requestor_principal, request_origin, correlation_id, outcome_status. Store in audit log stream.
2) Signed issuance proof — PKI-signed CSR receipt or SPIRE entry creation log with server signature.
3) Policy snapshot — the policy version (git sha) that authorized the issuance (RBAC policy and service-permission map).
4) Token or certificate thumbprint hash — SHA256 of the issued credential (not the credential itself) to avoid storing plaintext secrets.
5) Telemetry context — sampling of egress/ingress traces (trace_id, span context) correlating the identity use to client calls.
6) Automated verification runbook output — results of the automated post-issuance checks (mutual TLS handshake test, SPIFFE ID validation).

Evidence retention classification
--------------------------------
- EPHEMERAL (7 days): active credential payloads, full token bodies, and transient secrets. These must be purged by automated rotation workflows and never written permanently to persistent object stores.
- OPERATIONAL (90 days): event metadata records, signed issuance proofs, thumbprint hashes, and telemetry context. Used for incident investigation and operational troubleshooting.
- COMPLIANCE (3 years): policy snapshots, signed proofs, and curated audit slices required for periodic audits. Only hashes and signed receipts are kept, not raw secrets.
- LEGAL_HOLD (indefinite): artifacts subject to a legal hold. Legal holds override normal retention rules and must be coordinated with the Records & Legal team.

Owner responsibilities
----------------------
- Platform/SRE (owner): maintain automated collectors, ensure retention policies are enforced by object lifecycle rules, provide runbooks for evidence retrieval within SLA.
- Security (owner): approve the evidence schema and sampling budgets, run quarterly audits of evidence completeness, manage legal hold requests.
- Application teams: annotate service identity requests with business justification and owner contact. Participate in rotation drills when notified.

Audit and verification SLOs
--------------------------
- Evidence completeness: 99.5% of identity events must have the minimal evidence package within 5 minutes of issuance (measurement window: 30-day rolling).
- Retrieval SLA: evidence slices required for an internal investigation must be retrievable within 2 business days; for regulatory auditors within 5 business days.
- Tamper alerting: any modification to a stored signed issuance proof must raise a high-severity alert (PagerDuty and security channel).

Automation recipes and examples
------------------------------
1) Collector (SPIRE example) — high-level steps:
   - SPIRE server plugin emits a json line to the mesh-audit topic on issuance.
   - Kafka consumer running in the audit pipeline enriches the event with git tag of the policy repo and computes SHA256(cert) -> stores in operational store.
   - Retention lifecycle: object metadata set to OPERATIONAL with 90-day TTL.

Example pseudocode (collector):
```bash
# example: process a CSR-issued event and create operational evidence\jq '. as $e | { event_id: $e.id, identity_subject: $e.spiffeid, issuer_id: $e.issuer, timestamp_utc: $e.ts, outcome_status: $e.status }' < csr_event.json > evidence_record.json
sha256sum issued_cert.pem | awk '{print $1}' > cert_thumbprint.txt
# push to audit store (cli example)
redwood-audit-cli put --bucket identity-evidence --key events/${event_id}.json --body evidence_record.json --tags retention=operational
```

2) Istio / mTLS proof sampling policy (example YAML snippet):
```yaml
policy:
  name: mtls-evidence-sampling
  sampling_rate: 0.8  # sample 80% of issuance events for full telemetry context
  min_capture: 10     # at least 10 events per day
  capture_fields: ["trace_id","span_id","client_ip","server_ip","tls_cipher"]
  retention_class: operational
```

Chain-of-custody and cryptographic guarantees
--------------------------------------------
- Signed issuance proofs must be anchored in an immutable ledger (append-only storage) with SHA-256 chaining and periodic notarization to an external storage cold vault. Use object-store write-once flags and HMAC verification for transfer.
- Every evidence object must contain: created_by, created_at_utc, source_host, source_commit_sha, and a provenance_signature signed by the collector service identity key.

Incident response integration
-----------------------------
- Triage playbook excerpt for suspected identity compromise:
  1. Rotate impacted service identity (automated identity revoke + new issuance).
  2. Collect evidence slice: issuance proof, telemetry context, policy snapshot, and thumbprint hashes.
  3. Place related artifacts under LEGAL_HOLD if exfiltration is suspected.
  4. Run automated forensic checks (timeline reconstruction, lateral movement detection).
  5. Notify customers if MSP/tenant boundaries are affected per incident-comms policy.

Forensic checklist (fast reference)
---------------------------------
- Confirm issuance timestamp and issuer fingerprint.
- Validate policy version hash against git.
- Verify thumbprint of revoked certs matches observed network traces.
- Correlate trace_ids with affected service spans in tracing store (Jaeger/Tempo).

Evidence packaging for external audits
------------------------------------
When responding to an external audit, produce a curated bundle containing:
- A manifest (CSV) listing event_ids and artifact locations (S3 object paths).
- Signed issuance proofs (only receipts, not raw keys).
- Policy git commit SHAs and a signed git tag referencing the release.
- A short procedural narrative explaining collection windows and sampling rates.
- Redaction notes where raw secrets were excluded.

Example manifest row (CSV):
"event_id","type","path","retention_class","hash"
"evt-20250201-0001","issuance","s3://identity-evidence/events/evt-20250201-0001.json","operational","3b7f...c9a2"

Compliance exceptions and risk acceptance
---------------------------------------
- Exceptions: application teams may request an exception to store a raw short-lived token for integration testing. Exceptions must:
  - Be requested via the control-exception workflow (link to risk-and-exceptions registry).
  - Include a compensating control (KMS-wrapped, access-limited bucket, 7-day TTL).
  - Be approved by Security and Records teams.
- Risk acceptance: any accepted exception must be recorded in the global exception register with a business justification, approver, and expiry.

Operational runbooks and retrieval steps
--------------------------------------
1) Quick retrieval (internal investigation):
   - Use redwood-audit-cli search --event_id <id> --fields evidence_paths --output json
   - Run redwood-evidence-toolkit assemble --manifest <paths.csv> --output /tmp/audit-bundle.zip
2) For regulator request: follow the regulated export checklist and escalate to Security + Legal. Retrieve under a dedicated ephemeral environment; do not transfer raw secrets outside jurisdictional boundaries.

Monitoring and metrics
----------------------
Suggested metrics to instrument:
- identity_events_total (label=event_type)
- evidence_completeness_ratio (per-day)
- evidence_retrieval_latency_seconds (p95)
- evidence_integrity_alerts_total
